title: Detecting Lithium Through Correlative Microscopy in a Scanning Electron Microscope: From Rocks to Batteries
content: Non-destructive detection of lithium is a rather challenging task for standard methods such as EDS and WDS in a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) due to its low atomic number and quantum mechanical considerations [1,2]. On the other hand, lithium finds its applications in many industrial sectors such as: batteries, ceramics, glasses, lubricants, refrigeration, nuclear technologies, and photovoltaics. For many of these applications, high resolution imaging and knowledge of the various composing phases become crucial.
